language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi! My name is Tori, and I live in Seychelles. This is my brother Jacques. We both love football, I want to play for the Seychelles team some day.
I am studying about sound in school. Did you know that sound is a type of energy? It is made out of vibrations. These vibrations are called sound waves.
When the vibrating sound waves collide with particles, they make the particles vibrate too! When these particles are bumped, their vibrations carry the sound wave further.
Remember that everything is made up of particles, so sound waves can travel through any solid, liquid or gas!
If I bang these coconuts together, they will create a vibration that travels through the air as a sound wave.
Air is a gas. The sound waves travel though the particles in the air.
If sound waves collide with your ear and reach your ear drum, you will hear the sound that the waves carry.

That's great!
Let's get started!

That's great!
Let's get started!
Sound waves collide with the particles in solids, liquids and gases. Solids, liquids and gases are called the medium in which the sound waves travel.
The more particles there are in a medium, the longer the sound waves continue. The longer the sound waves continue, the further away the sound can be heard.
Dense solids, like the trunk of a coconut tree, are made up of particles that are packed very closely together. When one vibrates, the surrounding particles vibrate, too.
Liquids, like water, are make up of molecules that aren't so close together. The molecules move around, and have space between them. There are more particles to vibrate, but they are farther apart.
Gases, like air have molecules that are very far apart. There are not as many of them, and they move around even more than the particles in liquid do.

The particles in porous solids, like sponges, have holes filled with air
in them.

The length of a sound wave depends on the medium it travels through. Usually, a medium that has the most particles will carry sound the farthest. That means that the sound can be heard from the longest distance.

Can you help me figure out which medium lets sound waves travel
the farthest?

I learned that porous solids absorb sound because the sound waves are trapped by the holes in the medium. Sound can also be absorbed when there is a layer of air around dense solids.

On the forest floor, there are leaves that have fallen off of the trees. There is a layer of air in between the leaves. Sound waves are trapped in the air, just like they are trapped by the holes in porous solids.
